title: An early 15.052-day GJ 3341 residual wave does not reduce later SERVAL error in 74 HARPS exposures
abstract: We search early GJ 3341 HARPS velocities for an extra stable wave after a model for the known 14.207-day planet. The strongest early residual is at 15.051870 days. Its fixed early wave raises later corrected SERVAL squared error by 10.4% in 74 exposures. A conditional 30-day range for error reduction is -58.5% to +7.4%. DRS gives a small positive gain with a range that includes zero. Published A119 velocities give a negative point gain. The test finds no clear new planet candidate. One unflagged RVBank row has a large velocity departure in both reductions and is removed by a stated quality rule. The cause is not known. Signal recovery is low at 2 m/s, so this result does not exclude planets. All products share HARPS spectra. No independent instrument confirms a new signal. Code, frozen inputs, source hashes, controls, recovery trials, and offline steps are included.

display.caption: Early residual search, later conditional error ranges, later residuals, and injected-wave recovery. Negative gain means more squared error. The ranges hold all fitted coefficients fixed.

citations.reason: Provides context for a fixed early wave test. No code or data are reused.
